newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica to sign anti-drug pact with United States.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica to sign anti-drug pact with United States.

text.p: Jamaica is planning to sign a drug interdiction accord with the United States similar to those signed by other Caribbean states, but with more restrictions on U.S. movements in Jamaican territory, officials said.

Prime Minister P.J. Patterson, in an announcement late Sunday, said the accord would differ from those signed by nine other Caribbean states earlier this year in that U.S. officials would not be allowed to operate within the nation's territorial airspace or waters.
He said the accord would instead cover Jamaica's 188-square-mile (500 sq km) exclusive economic zone.

Jamaican officials have said the U.S. government has asked for a so-called "hot pursuit" agreement, which would allow U.S. drug enforcement officials to pursue suspected drug traffickers and apprehend them within Jamaican territory.
Patterson has said that the "hot pursuit" treaties are "inconsistent with Jamaica's sovereignty" and he had no intention of signing one.

In making the announcement on Sunday, Patterson noted Jamaica does not have the capacity to patrol the exclusive economic zone outside its 12-mile (19-km) limit and therefore was willing to allow the United States to operate in these waters in "clearly defined circumstances."
The United States does not recognise exclusive economic zones, maintaining they are international waters.
